planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in part sun to light shade after the last frost.

directions: This rarely-offered Japanese selection forms an evergreen clump of rounded leaves speckled with small yellow spots and marked by more sharply angular leaf ruffling than related spotted cultivars such as 'Kagami Jishi'. Site it in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in part sun to light shade, mulching to keep roots cool through Gulf Coast summer humidity; established clumps tolerate brief dry spells better than thinner-leaved farfugium but still benefit from supplemental water in drought. Yellow daisy-like flowers rise on stalks above the foliage starting in late October, extending fall interest and drawing butterflies. Use it as a specimen or textural accent among ferns and hostas in a shaded border.

common_name: Crazy Curls Leopard Plant (Deeply Cut Ruffled Farfugium)

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in consistently moist, rich soil in light shade to shade after the last frost.

directions: A 2024 Juniper Level Botanic Garden introduction selected from seedlings since 2018, this cultivar carries glossy, dark green, deeply cut and ruffled leaves that run roughly 7 inches long by 10 inches wide on a clump that spreads to a substantial 44 inches wide. Grow it in light shade to shade in humus-rich soil that stays evenly moist; it is noted as deer- and rabbit-resistant and adaptable to dry shade once established, making it forgiving under mature Gulf Coast tree canopies. In late October the clump sends up 30-inch flower spikes crowded with 2-inch yellow daisy-like blooms that draw pollinators well into fall. The heavily dissected leaf silhouette gives strong textural contrast against strappy-leaved shade companions like liriope or ferns.

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in consistently moist, rich soil in part sun to light shade after the last frost.

directions: A 2026 Juniper Level Botanic Garden introduction bred from a 2019 seed selection, Fandango forms a 15-inch clump of solid green leaves with slightly jagged margins, distinguishing it from spotted or heavily ruffled farfugium selections. Grow it in part sun to light shade in evenly moist, fertile soil; the sturdy, undemanding foliage tolerates Gulf Coast heat and humidity well and also performs as a container filler or tropical-look houseplant where winters run too cold for outdoor planting. Masses of double yellow flowers open on 2-foot stalks beginning in mid-October, offering more flower substance than the single-daisy blooms typical of the species. Use it in cottage-style shade borders or as a cut flower for fall arrangements.

common_name: Sweet Spot Dwarf Farfugium (Miniature Spotted Leopard Plant)

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in consistently moist, rich soil in part sun to light shade after the last frost; excellent in containers where winters run too cold for outdoor planting.

directions: A 2022 Juniper Level Botanic Garden introduction selected as a seedling of the dwarf cultivar 'Basho Ogi', Sweet Spot is even more diminutive than its already-small parent, maturing at just 5 inches tall and a foot wide with leaves under 3 inches across that are heavily spotted yellow. Grow it in part sun to light shade in humus-rich, evenly moist soil; its small root mass makes it prone to drying out faster than larger farfugium selections, so mulch well and water during Gulf Coast dry spells. Small clumps are topped by 1-foot spikes of yellow daisy flowers beginning in mid-October. Where winters exceed its hardiness, it thrives as a windowsill houseplant, and outdoors it fits neatly along shaded path edges or in rock gardens as a groundcover.

common_name: Wild One Leopard Plant (Serrate Ruffled-Leaf Farfugium)

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in consistently moist, rich soil in part sun to light shade after the last frost.

directions: A 2026 Juniper Level Botanic Garden introduction, Wild One carries bold, glossy green leaves that are both slightly serrate and ruffled along the margin, giving the clump extra textural movement compared to smooth-edged farfugium forms. Grow it in part sun to light shade in evenly moist, humus-rich soil; established plants tolerate the heat and humidity of Gulf Coast summers well and spread to a full 3 feet wide at maturity, making it useful as a bold groundcover under high shade. Starting in mid-October, 28-inch stalks of bright yellow daisies rise above the foliage for reliable fall color and butterfly visits. It also performs well as a container thriller or cut flower.

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in consistently moist, rich soil in sun to part sun after the last frost, allowing ample room for its very wide spread.

directions: A 2024 Juniper Level Botanic Garden introduction believed to be the largest-growing farfugium selection yet encountered, Lance-a-Lot originated from an all-green sport of a giant spotted leopard plant received from California plantsman Lance Reiners. Massive glossy green leaves 12 to 14 inches wide are held on very long petioles, and clumps spread to a full 5 feet wide at maturity, so give it ample room. It tolerates more sun than most farfugium selections, performing well from sun to part sun, and is noted as drought tolerant once established, a useful trait for Gulf Coast plantings that see periodic dry spells despite typically moist summers. Yellow-gold, daisy-like flowers appear in fall. Use it as a bold anchor specimen or dramatic groundcover beneath high, open shade.

directions: This 2024 Juniper Level Botanic Garden hybrid selection carries very dark evergreen leaves about 9 inches wide with greatly exaggerated, blunt lobes that create a striking illusion of depth against flatter-leaved farfugium companions, giving the cultivar its name. Grow it in part sun to light shade in humus-rich, evenly moist soil; the sturdy dark foliage holds its color and texture well through Gulf Coast summer heat and humidity. Starting in mid to late October, 30-inch flower stalks carry a dense show of 2-inch bright yellow daisies, extending seasonal interest into fall. Its dramatically lobed, shadow-casting leaves make it a strong focal point in a shaded foliage border.

common_name: Basho Ogi Leopard Plant (Dwarf Speckled Farfugium)

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in consistently moist, rich soil in part sun to light shade after the last frost.

directions: A little-known dwarf Japanese cultivar of the luchuense variety, Basho Ogi forms compact 8-inch clumps of unusually shaped 4-inch-long by 5-inch-wide leaves nicely speckled with yellow. It performs best in consistently moist, rich soil in part sun to light shade, appreciating the humidity of a Gulf Coast shade garden but needing more even moisture than larger, thicker-leaved farfugium selections. Beginning in mid-October, branched scapes of yellow aster-like flowers rise 2 feet above the low foliage clump. Its small stature and patterned leaves suit it to shaded rock gardens, container plantings, and path edges where a larger farfugium would overwhelm the space; it is also the parent of the even more diminutive cultivar 'Sweet Spot'.
